It's like I've killed myself and then used the decaying organs of my rotting corpse to build a new person without any problems, without any doubts or fears. It's LIBERATING. I've been LIBERATED. I am an organic nebula that is past its prime but is still churning out stars. I am a wartime weapons factory converted to luxury goods production. I am a 1968 Ford Mustang that sat in its owners garage for forty years and has now been restored to be even better than when it was new. I am Joe's Resurgent Phoenix. I am FREE.

Do you have any idea how easy life becomes when there's nothing to stop you? I don't even care anymore. I've let go of my doubts and fears. Gone. Out the window. I don't even care that I practically live in emotional squalor. I don't even care that I wake up every day on a mattress I can't afford to replace underneath a lamp too old to actually see anything in a room too cluttered to find peace. I don't even care that I spend every practical hour either wasting my life on a job with no purpose or wasting my life on silly avenues of entertainment that I can't really afford. I don't even care that I'll almost certainly die alone, with no one but my just-as-purposeless sister to attend my funeral. I don't even care that I'm the societal equivalent of damp toilet paper. I'm FREE. None of that matters because I'm FREE. I have almost nothing but my own brain, and that's all I need. I am nothing but a walking catalyst for my own actions, and that's all anybody really needs to survive.

I pitied a bird today. I saw one, a seagull, flying outside the window of the building where I work. I watched it hover in the air like an overused metaphor, and then land. I thought to myself how fucking terrible it must be to be a bird. To be able to fly, to be able to put the sky below you and ride it, but then be forced to land. Be forced to either abandon the sky or die. God that must suck.

I am not a bird. I am not a plane that makes routine stops on the ground despite being designed to fly. I am not a space shuttle that either returns to the earth in one piece or a thousand. No, I am a fucking solar beam. I'm a ray of light shooting out of the sun at a billion miles per hour and nothing can stop me. Even if I hit the ground I'll just bounce off and keep going at a billion miles an hour in some other direction. Even if I hit the end of the universe I'll just do an about face and keep going. I am raw fucking energy, radiating UV rays everywhere I step and giving myself a mental sunburn because of how fucking FREE I am.

I don't even care that I'm shivering right now because I can't afford to turn on the heat this early on in the year. I don't even feel the cold. My body is shivering because it's 59 degrees but my mind is experiencing the heat of a nuclear explosion, because my every thought is an atom bomb. Because I know that tomorrow, and tomorrow's tomorrow, and tomorrow's tomorrow's tomorrow could not possibly be worse than what I have already lived through. I have already been through my darkest hour. The healthy human mind, as I am told, does not revel in pain. I don't think it's painful. I think it's liberating. To know that no matter WHAT happens, no matter WHAT the world throws at you, it literally could NOT be worse than your own history...really puts things into fucking perspective, you know? But who's perspective? Ain't that the question? What does being LIBERATED really MEAN? I'll tell you what it means.

It means understanding that I wake up on a mattress that somebody else built, under a lamp built in a factory that I don't own. It means that my heat is powered by natural gas that somebody else fracked out of the earth. It means that my job is working for somebody else fixing somebody else's problems on streets paved by somebody else who gets paid by somebody else. It means that when I buy food cooked by somebody else, I'm paying with money printed by somebody else's mint. It means waking up knowing that you're breathing air breathed by a billion people and just as many animals before you. It means realizing that I wear clothes weaved by somebody else's machines, drive a car assembled in somebody else's factory that I bought from somebody else's dealership, and that I'm getting flats in somebody else's tires on potholes in somebody else's road as I follow a tractor trailer going to somebody else's destination.

It means understanding that I live in a world entirely dominated by actions of somebody else. I am nothing. I contribute nothing. My job could easily be filled by somebody else. I don't do anything particularly productive. The shitty 5-paragraph text files I submit to Bhutanese architecture forums aren't really making anybody think. Even if they did, they'd just be thinking somebody else's thoughts.

But I don't see that as a bad thing. I'm living in somebody else's world. And I think that's the best thing I could possibly do. Because of one simple reason. I don't OWE it anything and it doesn't OWE me anything. And that's liberating. It's liberating to understand that my doubts and fears were about somebody else's world. That my pain was about somebody else's problems. Not mine. Because I am only my brain. I am only my thoughts. Everything else is secondary.

If I became a quadriplegic tomorrow, I'd be a cripple based on somebody else's definition of the word. I'd be disabled based on somebody else's point of view. Me? I don't really see that as a problem. Because I can still think. It's impossible to be a poor thought. You can have poor thoughts, but you cannot BE one. So why the fuck would I care if I live a poor life in a poor world? I'm poor by somebody else's standards. Not mine.

So I'll go to work on Monday and I'll do a damn good job at it. Always do. Because now I have nothing to lose. I have literally nothing to lose by waking up at 4:30 AM and stumbling my way through a freeway. I have literally nothing to lose by watching another three people die in a single morning. What do I have to lose, really? Can a low wage take my thoughts away? Can a menial job with shitty hours drive me insane? No. No it can't. And THAT's why I'll always be free. Because I recognize that pain is fleeting. Fear is fleeting. Every catalyst fades. But I don't. Until the last syllable of my story I will still be my own protagonist. And because of that, I don't care about all the other subplots. They're irrelevant to me. I am a solar ray, illuminating my entire life, kindling fire in my soul. I'm a banner, unfurled and blown in the wind, spelling out my own FREEDOM to the rest of the world. I've no date with sorrow tonight, and I've already filed for divorce with pain.

But more than all of that, I've had enough for one day.
